lessons.0.slides.1.title: Côte de Beaune
lessons.0.slides.1.content: The Côte de Beaune lies south of the Côte de Nuits, stretching approximately 25 km from Corgolouin to Santenay. It is the world's foremost sanctuary for great white wine, while also producing elegant Pinot Noir.

lessons.0.slides.3.points.1: Chardonnay achieves its finest expression here

lessons.0.slides.5.title: 🏆 The Eight White Grand Crus
lessons.0.slides.5.points.0: Montrachet — 8 ha, king of white wine
lessons.0.slides.6.title: Why Are Côte de Beaune Whites So Great?
lessons.0.slides.6.content: A perfect convergence of terroir: limestone soils deliver minerality and vivid acidity; southeast-facing slopes capture ample sunshine; the cool climate preserves freshness; and centuries of mastery in Chardonnay viticulture and winemaking.

lessons.1.title: Montrachet — King of White Wine
lessons.1.slides.0.title: Montrachet Grand Cru
lessons.1.slides.0.subtitle: Lesson 2 - 20 minutes
lessons.1.slides.0.description: Explore the world's most expensive and complex white wine
lessons.1.slides.1.title: Montrachet
lessons.1.slides.1.content: Montrachet is the undisputed king of white wine — just 8 hectares, straddling Puligny and Chassagne. The wine combines power, elegance, and complexity in a way found nowhere else on earth, revealing unfathomable depth with age.
lessons.1.slides.2.title: Montrachet Family Grand Cru Map

lessons.1.slides.3.title: 👑 Montrachet Style
lessons.1.slides.3.points.0: Colour: deep gold, turning amber with age
lessons.1.slides.3.points.1: Aromas: white blossom, hazelnut, butter, honey, minerals
lessons.1.slides.3.points.2: Palate: full and round, silky texture
lessons.1.slides.3.points.4: Complexity: infinite layers, extraordinarily long finish
lessons.1.slides.3.points.6: Price: thousands to tens of thousands of USD per bottle

lessons.1.slides.6.title: 🏰 Top Producers
lessons.1.slides.7.title: Tasting Recommendations
lessons.1.slides.7.content: Montrachet needs time to open up — ideally aged at least 5–10 years. Serve at 12–14 °C in a large Burgundy white wine glass, and decant for 30–60 minutes. Young bottles often go through a closed phase; patience is richly rewarded.

lessons.2.title: Meursault — Land of Gold
lessons.2.slides.0.title: Meursault Village

lessons.2.slides.0.description: Explore Burgundy's most celebrated white wine village
lessons.2.slides.1.title: Meursault
lessons.2.slides.1.content: Meursault has no Grand Cru, yet it is home to some of Burgundy's finest Premier Cru vineyards. Its whites are celebrated for their creamy texture, hazelnut aromas, and rich palate — the archetype of 'golden Burgundy'.
lessons.2.slides.2.title: Meursault Village Map
lessons.2.slides.2.description: Click to explore the boundaries of Meursault
lessons.2.slides.3.title: 🍯 Meursault White Style
lessons.2.slides.3.points.1: Aromas: hazelnut, butter, toasted almond, honey
lessons.2.slides.3.points.2: Palate: full and round, buttery smooth
lessons.2.slides.3.points.3: Acidity: soft yet sufficient for balance
lessons.2.slides.3.points.6: Appeal: more approachable than Montrachet, more affordable
lessons.2.slides.4.title: 💎 Distinguished Premier Crus
lessons.2.slides.4.points.0: Les Perrières — closest to Grand Cru quality
lessons.2.slides.4.points.1: Les Genevrières — elegant with fine minerality
lessons.2.slides.4.points.2: Les Charmes — charming, as the name suggests
lessons.2.slides.5.title: Meursault vs. Puligny-Montrachet
lessons.2.slides.6.title: Value for Money
lessons.2.slides.6.content: Premier Cru Meursault is an ideal introduction to top-level Burgundy white wine. A Les Perrières or Les Genevrières from a great producer approaches Grand Cru quality at a considerably more accessible price.

lessons.3.title: Corton Hill — Dual Excellence
lessons.3.slides.0.title: Corton Hill Grand Crus
lessons.3.slides.0.subtitle: Lesson 4 - 16 minutes
lessons.3.slides.0.description: Explore the only red Grand Cru zone of the Côte de Beaune
lessons.3.slides.1.title: Corton Hill
lessons.3.slides.1.content: Corton Hill is an isolated hill at the northern end of the Côte de Beaune, spanning three villages. It produces both the powerful red Grand Cru Corton and the refined white Grand Cru Corton-Charlemagne.
lessons.3.slides.2.title: Corton Hill Grand Cru Map
lessons.3.slides.2.description: Click to explore the red and white Grand Crus of Corton
lessons.3.slides.3.title: 🏔️ Corton Hill Features
lessons.3.slides.3.points.0: Spans three villages: Aloxe-Corton, Pernand-Vergelesses, Ladoix
lessons.3.slides.3.points.1: Red Grand Cru: Corton (160 ha — Burgundy's largest)
lessons.3.slides.3.points.3: Legend: Charlemagne the Great once owned these vineyards
lessons.3.slides.3.points.4: Topography: each face of the hill expresses a different style
lessons.3.slides.4.title: 🍷 Corton Red
lessons.3.slides.4.points.0: Style: between Côte de Nuits and Côte de Beaune
lessons.3.slides.4.points.1: Aromas: red and black fruit, spice, forest floor
lessons.3.slides.4.points.2: Palate: powerful yet not without elegance
lessons.3.slides.5.title: 🥂 Corton-Charlemagne White
lessons.3.slides.5.points.0: Aromas: white blossom, lemon, flint, minerals
lessons.3.slides.5.points.1: Palate: elegant and precise, vibrant acidity
lessons.3.slides.5.points.4: Distinction: leaner and more refined than Montrachet
lessons.3.slides.5.points.5: Price: more accessible than Montrachet but outstanding quality
lessons.3.slides.6.title: Investment Perspective
lessons.3.slides.6.content: Corton-Charlemagne is an outstanding choice for investing in top Burgundy whites — priced 30–50% below Montrachet, yet matching it in ageing potential and complexity. Leading producers include Bonneau du Martray and Coche-Dury.

lessons.4.title: Côte de Beaune Reds
lessons.4.slides.0.title: Côte de Beaune Red Wine Villages
lessons.4.slides.0.subtitle: Lesson 5 - 14 minutes
lessons.4.slides.0.description: Explore the elegant reds of Pommard, Volnay, and beyond
lessons.4.slides.1.title: Pommard
lessons.4.slides.1.content: Pommard is one of the Côte de Beaune's most celebrated red wine villages, renowned for its powerful, masculine style. It has no Grand Cru but boasts 28 Premier Crus — wines that demand patience and age.
lessons.4.slides.2.title: Pommard and Volnay Map
lessons.4.slides.2.description: Click to see the locations of these two red wine villages
lessons.4.slides.3.title: 💪 Pommard Style
lessons.4.slides.3.points.1: Aromas: black fruit, animal leather, spice
lessons.4.slides.3.points.5: Notable Premier Crus: Les Rugiens, Les Epenots
lessons.4.slides.4.title: Volnay
lessons.4.slides.4.content: In sharp contrast to neighbouring Pommard, Volnay is the Côte de Beaune's most elegant red. The Pinot Noir here shows a silky texture and floral character — often called 'the Chambolle-Musigny of red wines'.
lessons.4.slides.5.title: 🌹 Volnay Style
lessons.4.slides.5.points.2: Palate: silky and refined, soft tannins
lessons.4.slides.5.points.3: Elegance: the highest in the Côte de Beaune
lessons.4.slides.6.title: Pommard vs. Volnay
lessons.4.slides.7.title: Côte de Beaune Reds Summary
lessons.4.slides.7.content: Overall, Côte de Beaune reds are more elegant and approachable than their Côte de Nuits counterparts, yet top Premier Crus — such as Pommard Les Rugiens and Volnay Caillerets — rival the best in quality while offering greater value.
